dossier.public_summary: The dip changes depth by about 98% between sectors and is weaker between the two good TESS-SPD detections, with only five transits near a gap. Its 3-hour duration is 1.6 times too long for a central transit on this small M dwarf, and the star shows no sign that a planet explains this behaviour. Together this is best explained by noise and systematics, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by ~98% between sectors (per_sector: 2879±1312, 11027±1699, 10925±1004 ppm); sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with TESS-SPOC p_constant 0.00014719893639390016, so the signal is not stable even within one pipeline.
Refit snr 11.84 is puffed by a few events; the dip is carried by only ~44.6% from the top three of five transits with a small number of transits near a gap, inconsistent with a periodic planet.

1.61× central duration with stellar_density_penalty 37.13 and star_density_penalty_share 0.2596 indicates the shape does not match the stellar density; flat bottom v_sigma -1.598 does not offset this.
reasons.value: 1.612 on an M dwarf (rad 0.2565, Teff 3279 K), central_h 1.86 vs observed_h 2.999

reasons.why: Low machine-learned rank and marginal secondary (depth_ppm 1344, depth_over_dip 0.1567) alongside no secondary at half period and no odd/even difference (0.3037) leave no positive planet signature to outweigh the depth instability and duration mismatch.
reasons.value: planet_rank 0.07, phase_curve chi2 7.487 dof 9, secondary snr 2.455
